content.value_statement: Prisma Next runtime setup can fail through incorrect imports, middleware order, or connection lifecycle choices. This skill provides target-specific, typed configuration guidance.
actual_capabilities: Creates typed db.ts patterns for Postgres, SQLite, and Mongo runtime facades.
Explains ordered composition for telemetry, lint, and budget middleware.
Configures DATABASE_URL, pool options, and environment-specific middleware behavior.
Shows transaction patterns for Postgres and SQLite while identifying Mongo limitations.
Explains connection teardown for scripts and persistent singleton clients for servers.
limitations: It does not design contracts or write application queries.
It does not provide built-in read-replica or multi-database routing.
Mongo clients do not expose SQL surfaces or the documented transaction helper.
Some PostgreSQL pool options require a separately constructed pg.Pool.

use_cases.title: Create a runtime entry point
use_cases.description: Generate a typed db.ts for a selected database target with correct contract imports and environment configuration.
use_cases.target_user: Application developers starting a Prisma Next project

use_cases.title: Add runtime safeguards
use_cases.description: Compose telemetry, lint, and budget middleware in an intentional order with verified option names.

use_cases.title: Fix connection lifecycle issues
use_cases.description: Choose correct client ownership and teardown patterns for servers, scripts, workers, and continuous integration tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a typed Prisma Next db.ts for {target} using my emitted contract and DATABASE_URL.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one database target

prompt_templates.title: Add middleware
prompt_templates.prompt: Add telemetry, lints, and budgets to my Prisma Next runtime with safe defaults and explain the middleware order.

prompt_templates.title: Configure environments
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my db.ts for development and production, keeping secrets external and changing middleware through NODE_ENV.

prompt_templates.title: Review lifecycle architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this server and script database setup for pool ownership, transaction support, teardown behavior, and target-specific limitations.

output_examples.input: Set up Prisma Next with PostgreSQL and telemetry.
output_examples.output: A typed runtime plan with the PostgreSQL facade, contract artifacts, DATABASE_URL, telemetry first, and a process-level singleton.

output_examples.input: My one-off PostgreSQL script finishes queries but never exits.
output_examples.output: A teardown recommendation using db.close after pending work, with await using reserved for the top level of short-lived scripts.

output_examples.input: Switch my runtime from PostgreSQL to MongoDB.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist covering the Mongo facade, re-emitted artifacts, collection addressing, and unavailable SQL and transaction surfaces.

best_practices: Keep DATABASE_URL in environment configuration and never commit credentials.
Place telemetry outermost when it must observe lint and budget failures.
Use one module-level client for servers and close clients only in short-lived scripts.
anti_patterns: Do not construct and dispose a database client inside every request handler.
Do not invent middleware package paths or unsupported option names.
Do not assume Postgres, SQLite, and Mongo expose identical query and transaction surfaces.

faq.question: Which databases are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Prisma Next runtime setup for Postgres, SQLite, and Mongo.

faq.question: Does it create Prisma contracts?
faq.answer: No. Use the dedicated contract skill to edit or generate contract definitions.

faq.question: Can it configure middleware?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers telemetry, lints, budgets, ordering, and verified option names.

faq.question: Does Mongo support db.transaction?
faq.answer: No. The documented transaction helper is available for Postgres and SQLite only.

faq.question: Why does my script stay running?
faq.answer: A PostgreSQL pool can keep the event loop active. Await pending work, then call db.close.

faq.question: Should a server close the client after each request?
faq.answer: No. Keep a module-level singleton alive for the process lifetime.
